body:
# The Kēr file: from ker to the temple it became
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Kēr** is what the evidence put back.

Kēr has no coherent biography because she is not a person but a function: the personification of the moment death happens. She appears most vividly in the Iliad. In the Iliad, the kēres hover over combat, eager to seize the souls of the fallen.  They are compared to vultures and carrion birds.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Kēr
- **ASCII form:** ker
- **Meaning:** "Doom, violent death (from κήρ)"
- **Domain of influence:** Violent Death, Doom, Fate
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Κήρ
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 130 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Κήρ**. On the evidence, it means "Doom, violent death (from κήρ)".

Strip **Kēr** to *ker* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **e → ē** — Macron: long eta: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Kēr** lives at [/sites/ker/](/sites/ker/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/ker/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/ker/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/ker/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Kēr** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Funerary & Memorial Services** — Doom at the battlefield’s edge.
- **Defense, Military & Security** — The kēres hover over every Iliadic battlefield, dragging off the fallen; war's death-toll personified.
- **Gaming, Fantasy & Entertainment IP** — Fantasy and role-playing games adopted the kēres wholesale as winged death-spirits.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/ker/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.

Continue the series — previous file: **Kārttikeya** ([read it here](/sites/kartikeya/blog/restoration/)) · next file: **Kōbe** ([read it here](/sites/kobe/blog/restoration/)).

*The Restoration Files are written from the same canonical record as the temples themselves: the lexicon, the lore catalog, the pattern atlas, and the cited scholarly sources. If a file ever disagrees with its temple, the temple is right — tell us, and the file will be corrected.*
